text:
GENERATE BURST T5P-A — Run C-9 test T5 (Matt R-C9-66): the PAINTED TEXTURE of the 3D manticore, step 1: its eight views. task_id "T5P-A".

IMAGE 1 is a sheet of EIGHT VIEWS of ONE 3D model of a four-legged creature standing still in one neutral pose, seen from eight directions around it at the same slight downward angle, on flat pure #00ff00. Top row, left to right: seen from BEHIND (north); facing away to the upper right (north-east); facing away to the upper left (north-west); facing the viewer's LEFT in profile (west). Bottom row, left to right: facing the viewer's RIGHT in profile (east); facing the lower right (south-east); facing the lower left (south-west); FACING THE VIEWER (south). They are renders of the model: every OUTLINE, POSITION and SIZE is correct and must not change; the surface is flat and plastic.
IMAGE 2 is the APPROVED character sheet of this creature, the MANTICORE: its lean hound body with ribs showing, blue-grey hide with a darker spine and paler belly, clawed paws, the long whip tail, the calm bearded, long-haired face of a MAN with a mane around it; and the painter's hand (dark ink line, hatching, transparent washes). IMAGE 3 is the 13th-century bestiary page it comes from: the face and its calm.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and deliver ONE 1536x1024 sheet in which EVERY view is repainted as the manticore of IMAGE 2 seen from that direction, inside exactly that view's outline, position and size.
THIS PAINTING BECOMES THE MODEL'S TEXTURE: it will be projected back onto the 3D model from these eight directions and the views are blended together. So:
1. ONE creature: the same hide colour, markings, ribs, mane, face and paws in every view. A marking that moves between views shows as a seam or a double.
2. Paint the SURFACE, not the lighting: soft even light as the register card says; no cast shadows, no dark side, no rim light, no shading that belongs to one viewpoint. Tone comes from the hide's own colours and the pen hatching.
3. Stay inside the outlines: do not paint beyond a silhouette and do not change a leg, tail or head outline.
HEAD: paint the face only where IMAGE 1 shows it (the front, the two front three-quarters and the two profiles). In the view from behind and the two rear three-quarters, paint the back of the head, the hair and the mane, with no face.

BACKGROUND: keep the background flat pure #00ff00, as in IMAGE 1. If the image model returns a darker or gradient background anyway, DO NOT spend a retry on it and still deliver the image: the figures are cut out afterwards by their exact 3D outlines, so the background colour does not decide success. Spend retries ONLY on the faults named below.
STYLE: the REGISTER CARD above is satisfied BY IMAGE 2: copy its hand; do not restyle.

Two image_gen EDIT calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if a view's outline, facing or position changed, a view is missing, the creature differs between views, or a face is painted on a head turned away — name the reason. Never retry for the background colour. Copy outputs to out/T5P-A_a.png and out/T5P-A_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "T5P-A"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the sheet to EDIT (eight views of the Meshy 3D manticore at rest, 19.77 deg; outlines correct, surface flat)
IMAGE 2 — the approved four-view character sheet of the manticore (look, markings, face, hand)
IMAGE 3 — the bestiary source (Rochester Bestiary, c.1230, public domain): the face and its calm
